newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa springs out of negative trend, seen up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa springs out of negative trend, seen up.

text.p: London cocoa futures burst out of a negative chart pattern in a fierce rally on Wednesday, technically clearing the way for further gains, traders said.
A strong close on the benchmark March cocoa suggested that the market may have secured its position above a downtrend channel that kept a stiff lid on gains in the past month.
Helped by follow through buying in New York, March cocoa jumped to a session high of 931 stg a tonne, then closed slightly lower at 928 stg -- a gain of 15 stg on the day.

Traders said New York's strong performance stimulated short covering and trade buying in London. Sterling's continued strength put a dampener on as it attracted West Afican origins but demand outpaced supply. "The technical picture looks much more positive now," said one trader.
Turnover on the exchange totalled a moderate 5,611 lots including a large volume of crosses and AAs.
"There was a lot of tidying up going on," said one.
On the switches Dec/March traded at a weaker 36 stg a tonne.

Early deals met resistance around 927 stg as commission houses and speculators jumped in to take profits. But the market regained momentum as New York's March contract smoothly cruised through the technically sensitive $1,390 level.
Sterling's rides against other European currencies continued to cripple business in the physical market. Cocoa was arriving in small quantities in Amsterdam and differentials were weakening.
Ivorian cocoa for January shipment was being offered at 20-25 stg under the London March futures contract while December was bought at 25 stg under, and was offered at 17.
On the futures, technical support is now at 920 stg -- which is where March can first meet the upper wall of the downtrend channel. Mild resistance is near and above 940.
